chapters.title: Architectural Foundation & Execution Mechanics
chapters.content: React operates as a declarative component-based rendering library that abstracts direct Document Object Model manipulation through a sophisticated virtual reconciliation layer. By utilizing concurrent rendering paradigms, the library orchestrates asynchronous update queues, allowing high-priority user interactions to interrupt low-priority background yields without blocking the main execution thread. The introduction of React Fiber restructured the core execution engine from a recursive stack-based architecture to a dynamic linked-list traversal mechanism. This fundamental shift empowers runtime schedulers to pause, abort, or resume rendering work incrementally across multiple frames, optimizing browser paint cycles. Furthermore, the decoupling of the renderer from core reconciliation algorithms enables React to target diverse execution targets seamlessly, ranging from traditional web DOM environments via ReactDOM to native mobile hardware through React Native abstractions. Memory management relies heavily on efficient memoization strategies and immutable state update patterns, preventing unnecessary tree diffing operations while maintaining deterministic component lifecycles across complex enterprise applications.
